name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Irwin's large fundraising and cash advantage over Gallucci
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but party hold is favored
model.rationale: The district's D+9 lean and a favorable national environment point to a solid Democratic hold, and Jacqui Irwin has outraised Sam Gallucci by more than two to one with outside support and no opposition spending against her. Markets price a Democratic win around 95%, consistent with a Safe D call despite the open seat.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or unusually strong GOP turnout could narrow the margin, though a Democratic loss remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Julia Brownley's retirement leaves this Ventura County-area seat open, but the district carries a nine-point Democratic lean and Democrats have held it comfortably. State Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin enters the general with a clear financial edge, having raised roughly $822,000 to Sam Gallucci's $377,000, and she holds a large cash-on-hand advantage while benefiting from outside support with none opposed.

Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances near 95%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing, all of which point to a Democratic hold in the mid-to-high teens.
